# browser-mcp

A Playwright-backed Model Context Protocol server providing browser primitives + domain plugins for design audits, WordPress block development, and Gutenberg authoring. Tools are grouped into modes; modes are registered by plugins.

This file is the consumer-facing reference for agents that *invoke* browser-mcp tools. If you're building or extending the server itself, read the source — this file deliberately omits implementation detail in favor of the contract surface that drives correct usage.

## TL;DR {#tldr}

- Browser primitives (navigate, click, screenshot, evaluate, ...) plus four pluggable domains: `dev`, `design-compare`, `wp`, `wp-gutenberg`.
- Plugins register **modes** (e.g. `wordpress`, `design`); `mcp__browser__list_modes` enumerates what's active in the current process.
- Tools accept an optional `session_id` to attach to a persistent context (from `open_session`); without it each call spins an ephemeral session and discards it on return.
- Comparison tools (`compare_element`, `compare_screenshot`, `visual_diff`, `design_audit`) report different score conventions and accept different mask APIs — see § Cross-cutting concepts before mixing them.
- All coordinates the tool produces or consumes are **HTML viewport pixels**. Values from Figma source carry their own coordinate frame and must be converted before they cross the API boundary — see § Coordinate spaces.
- This document tracks browser-mcp main; for behavior at a specific commit see `git log src/`. The fields documented here are stable as of commit 5078684 (maskCoverage on compare_element/compare_screenshot).

## Modes and plugin model {#modes-and-plugins}

The server boots with a plugin set defined by the `BROWSER_MCP_PLUGINS` env var (comma-separated, e.g. `dev,wp,wp-gutenberg,design-compare`). Each plugin can:

- Register tools (the `mcp__browser__*` surface).
- Register modes (named bundles that group tool capabilities, e.g. the `wordpress` mode requires `wp` and `wp-gutenberg` plugins).
- Declare required env vars and dependencies on other plugins.

**Tolerant loader.** A plugin with a missing required env var is silently skipped and its dependents cascade-skipped (e.g. `wp-gutenberg` skips when `wp` skips for missing `WP_URL`). Stderr carries the warning; the server still boots and the unaffected plugins still work. Hard errors only fire on real config bugs (sealed registry, name collision, undeclared dependency, tool/action/mode collision).

> **Hazard:** if `mcp__browser__list_modes` returns "No modes registered" or `wordpress` is missing, the cause is almost always a silently-skipped plugin from missing env. See `wp-mode-not-registered` in § Diagnosis for the fix recipe.

**MCP scopes replace, do not merge.** When the same server name (`browser`) appears in both `~/.claude.json` (user scope) and a project-local `.mcp.json`, the project entry **fully replaces** the user entry. There is no env-block merge. If a project needs a different `WP_URL`, the project entry must duplicate the full env block, not just the override.

**Where plugins live in source.** `src/plugins/dev`, `src/plugins/design-compare`, `src/plugins/wp`, `src/plugins/wp-gutenberg`. Plugin manifests at `src/plugins/<name>/index.ts`. Tool implementations under `src/plugins/<name>/tools/` (or `src/core/` for primitives). The plugin registry (`src/plugins/registry.ts`) enforces the dependency graph and the cascade-skip behavior.

## Command index {#command-index}

Exhaustive list of `mcp__browser__*` tools by plugin. Tools marked **(contract)** have a deep treatment in § Surfaces; the rest are routine and have a one-line entry only. Use this table to pick the right tool, then dive to the contract section if the tool is non-trivial.

### dev plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `screenshot` | Full-page or clipped PNG screenshot | core primitive |
| `element_screenshot` | Element-bbox-cropped screenshot | core primitive |
| `visual_diff` | Pixelmatch two PNGs, optional crop | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `compare_screenshot` | Live URL ↔ reference PNG, full-page | (contract) compare-tool selection, mask, coverage |
| `compare_element` | Live URL ↔ reference PNG, element-cropped | (contract) compare-tool selection, mask, alignment, coverage |
| `console_capture` | Capture console messages over a script run | |
| `dom_snapshot` | Full DOM tree as JSON | |
| `accessibility_snapshot` | a11y tree | |
| `network_log` | HAR-style network requests over a script run | |
| `page_metadata` | Title, URL, meta tags | |
| `performance_metrics` | LCP, FCP, TTFB | |
| `computed_styles` | `getComputedStyle()` for selector | |
| `evaluate_script` | Run JS in page context, return result | |
| `trace_start` / `trace_stop` | Playwright trace zip | |
| `schema_extract` | JSON-LD / microdata / OG tags | |

### design-compare plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `design_compare` | CSS-property comparison live ↔ design spec | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `design_audit` | `design_compare` + visual diff + cross-reference | (contract) compare-tool selection, hide, coverage |

### wp plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `wp` | WordPress admin login + REST helpers | requires `WP_URL`; optional `WP_USERNAME` / `WP_PASSWORD` |

### wp-gutenberg plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `insert_block` | Add a block to current post | depends on `wp` |
| `get_blocks` | Read current post's block tree | |
| `screenshot_block` | Crop screenshot to block bbox | |
| `inspect_toolbar` | Block toolbar state | |
| `compare_block` | `compare_element` scoped to a block | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `evaluate` | JS in editor iframe context | |
| `check_block` | Validity / breakage check | |
| `publish` | Save + publish current post | |
| `block_html` | Block's serialized HTML | |
| `clear_blocks` | Empty the post | |

### Session / navigation primitives (every plugin)

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `open_session`, `close_session`, `list_sessions` | persistent context lifecycle |
| `open_tab`, `switch_tab`, `list_tabs`, `close_tab` | tab control inside a session |
| `navigate`, `go_back`, `go_forward`, `reload` | URL navigation |
| `click`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `hover`, `scroll`, `drag` | input |
| `select_option`, `check`, `uncheck`, `upload_file` | form control |
| `wait`, `wait_for_selector`, `wait_for_url`, `wait_for_load_state` | sync |
| `get_text`, `get_attribute`, `get_html`, `get_url` | read |
| `get_cookies`, `set_cookies`, `clear_cookies` | cookies |
| `get_storage`, `set_storage`, `clear_storage` | localStorage / sessionStorage |
| `capture`, `save_pdf`, `save_html` | output capture |
| `handle_next_dialog` | pre-arm a confirm/alert handler |
| `list_modes` | enumerate registered modes |

## Cross-cutting concepts {#cross-cutting}

### Coordinate spaces {#coordinate-spaces}

> **Self-contained callout (mirrors `../figexport/llms-full.txt#coordinate-spaces`):** values from json carry their source coordinate frame; conversion to HTML viewport is the consumer's responsibility, not auto-resolved.

browser-mcp deals exclusively in **HTML viewport pixels** at every API boundary:

- `getBoundingClientRect()` — what the tool internally calls — returns viewport-relative coordinates, post-transform.
- The reference PNG passed to `compare_element` / `compare_screenshot` is treated as image-pixel space, which is 1:1 with HTML viewport when the screenshot was captured at the same dimensions (the tool defaults `viewport` to the reference image's dimensions to enforce this).
- `ignoreRegions[].x/y/width/height` — passed in image-pixel coords.
- `alignOn.referenceRect` — passed in image-pixel coords.
- `coverageManifest` — names and counts only; no coordinates.

**Conversion-hazard direction.** Figma source files (`design-context.json`, `tree.md`, design-styles.json) carry coordinates in either Figma canvas space, Figma node-relative space, or rendered HTML viewport — three distinct frames. figexport's authoritative treatment lives at `../figexport/llms-full.txt#coordinate-spaces`. browser-mcp **never** auto-resolves between frames — values pasted into `alignOn.referenceRect` from a Figma `absoluteBoundingBox` will silently absorb the canvas-vs-viewport offset into `deltaX`/`deltaY` and the comparison drifts. Named: `align-on-frame-mismatch`.

### Compare-tool selection {#compare-tool-selection}

When sources of truth disagree about which compare tool to use, the precedence is:

| Goal | Primary | Secondary | Tertiary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Live block ↔ Figma reference, with property checks | `design_audit` | `design_compare` + `compare_element` separately | `compare_screenshot` | `design_audit` runs both phases and cross-references clusters to elements |
| Live element ↔ static reference image | `compare_element` | `compare_screenshot` with `ignoreRegions` | `visual_diff` after manual capture | `compare_element` anchors on selector bbox; full-page only when bbox routing fails |
| Two static PNGs, no live page | `visual_diff` | — | — | no browser launched |
| Single CSS-property check, no visual diff needed | `design_compare` | `computed_styles` + manual assert | — | `design_compare` evaluates whole element list; `computed_styles` is one-shot |

**Score conventions differ.** This is the most common cross-tool misread:

- `compare_element`, `compare_screenshot`, `visual_diff` report **`Diff: N.NN%`** (lower = better) plus `Match: YES/NO` against `maxDiffPercent` (default 5%).
- `design_audit` reports **`visualScore`** computed as `1 - diffPercentage/100`, range `[0, 1]`, 4 decimals (higher = better).
- `pixelmatch` threshold knob: `precise` (0.1, default for `compare_*`) or `design` (0.3, default for `design_audit`). The threshold is per-pixel sensitivity, not the score.

### Mask contract {#mask-contract}

`compare_element` and `compare_screenshot` accept pixelmatch-time mask flags:

- `ignoreImages` / `ignoreBackgrounds` — by element kind. img tags / `background-image` rules.
- `ignoreAllImages` — `ignoreImages + ignoreBackgrounds`.
- `ignoreText` — every text-line bbox via TreeWalker + Range.getClientRects.
- `ignoreElements: [{selector, mode}]` — by selector; `mode` is `"invisible"` (alpha 0) or `"position-only"` (gray fill, position still verified).
- `ignoreRegions: [{x, y, width, height, mode?, reason?}]` — manual rects.

Mask bboxes are **re-collected on every call** at the moment between screenshot capture and the post-screenshot evaluate. They follow the live element's current position. Manual `ignoreRegions` rects are static and do not.

> **Hazard (`race-on-animation`):** the screenshot via Playwright's `page.screenshot()` and the bbox query via a subsequent `page.evaluate()` are two sequential awaits with no synchronization barrier. An element animating between them desyncs the mask from the screenshot. Mitigation: inject a freeze stylesheet via `actions: [{type: "evaluate", expression: "document.head.appendChild(...)"}]` (browser-mcp has no `freezeAnimations` flag on `compare_element`/`compare_screenshot`; `design_audit` does), or use `delay` past the longest in-flight transition, or double-capture and verify ≥ 0.99 inter-screenshot diff.

> **Hazard (`mask-pair-fabrication`):** `ignoreAllImages: true` AND `ignoreText: true` simultaneously on a content-heavy block masks ~all visible content; the comparison becomes wrapper-vs-wrapper and trivially scores 99%+. The tool reports `Mask coverage: N.N%` and emits a warning when coverage > 60% with both flags active. SKILL § 6.7 hard-fails this combination.

### Hide contract (design_audit only) {#hide-contract}

`design_audit` accepts:

- `hideSelectors: [selector]` — applies `visibility: hidden` BEFORE screenshot. Pixels are absent from the PNG entirely. `hiddenArea` reported as % of root area.
- `knownExclusions: [selector]` — post-hoc cluster classification, not masking. Diff clusters overlapping these elements get `status: "excluded"` instead of `"unexplained"`. No effect on the screenshot itself.

**`design_audit` does NOT support the `compare_element` mask API.** No `ignoreElements`, `ignoreAllImages`, `ignoreText`, or `ignoreRegions`. A builder searching for `ignoreText` on `design_audit` is making a category error — the analogue is `hideSelectors`, with a different mechanism (pre-screenshot suppression) and a different gate (`hiddenArea > 25%` hard-fail).

### Alignment contract {#alignment-contract}

`compare_element` accepts two mutually-exclusive alignment modes for shifting the reference crop to match the live element:

- `alignTo: "top" | "center"` — element-relative. Shifts the reference so the element's bbox lands at top-left or center.
- `alignOn: {referenceRect, frontendSelector, mode?}` — anchor-pair. Shifts the reference so a named anchor in both sides aligns.

Both compute `deltaX` / `deltaY` and apply that to the reference crop origin. `alignOn` warns when the delta exceeds 100px (`anchorOverThreshold`).

> **Hazard (`align-on-frame-mismatch`):** `alignOn.referenceRect` is consumed as image-pixel coords (HTML viewport, 1:1 with the reference PNG). If a builder pastes Figma-canvas coordinates here (e.g. `absoluteBoundingBox` from `design-context.json`), the canvas-vs-viewport offset becomes part of `deltaX`/`deltaY` and the comparison silently drifts. The 100px warning catches gross cases but not subtle ones.

### Coverage contract {#coverage-contract}

Both `compare_element`/`compare_screenshot` and `design_audit` surface coverage metrics, but with different semantics:

- `compare_element` / `compare_screenshot`: **`Mask coverage: N.N%`** — % of the comparison region (cropW × cropH for `compare_element`, full pageImg for `compare_screenshot`) covered by the union of mask regions, dedup-merged via bitmap. 1 decimal precision.
- `design_audit`: **`hiddenArea`** — % of `rootSelector`'s area covered by `hideSelectors` matches, naive sum (no dedup; overlapping selectors over-count). 1 decimal precision.
- `design_audit.coverageManifest`: takes `nodeNames: string[]` and `propertyCounts: {[name]: number}` (from figexport's `resolve_styles _meta`); reports per-element coverage stats and unmapped node count.

Both metrics are percentages, both 1 decimal. SKILL gates: `maskCoverage > 60%` with both broad mask flags = mask-pair-fabrication fingerprint; `hiddenArea > 25%` = independent hard-fail.

### Action contract {#action-contract}

`compare_element`, `compare_screenshot`, `design_audit`, and `screenshot` accept `actions: [...]` arrays that run before the capture. Action types:

- `click`, `type`, `hover`, `scroll`, `wait`, `wait_for_selector`, `assert_text`, `assert_count`, `evaluate`, `set_storage`, `set_cookies`, `select_option`, etc.

Assertions inside `actions` produce `assertions` output messages but don't fail the call by themselves. The `evaluate` action is the workaround route for animation-freezing on tools that lack `freezeAnimations` — pass a `<style>` injection that pauses animations and disables transitions.

### Session contract {#session-contract}

- `open_session({ browser, viewport })` returns `session_id`. The session keeps a Playwright `BrowserContext` alive across calls.
- All primitives accept optional `session_id` + `tab_id`. Without `session_id`, the tool spins an ephemeral context per call.
- `close_session({ session_id })` releases the context; `list_sessions()` enumerates active ones.

> **Hazard:** ephemeral sessions cannot accept cookies, storage, or auth state from prior calls — every ephemeral call is a fresh anonymous browser. For multi-step flows that need persistence (login → action → capture), open a session and pass `session_id` to every call.

## Surfaces {#surfaces}

Surface granularity is **per contract**, not per tool. Tools that share a contract (e.g. all four compare tools share the mask contract) point to one section. Tools without a contract entry are routine — see § Command index.

### compare_element {#surface-compare-element}

**Available in mode:** `dev` plugin — always present.

**Authoritative for:** live ↔ reference PNG comparison anchored on a CSS selector. Crop window auto-derived from `getBoundingClientRect() + padding` (default 50px). Masking, alignment, coverage reporting all flow through this tool.

**Not authoritative for:** full-page comparisons (use `compare_screenshot`); CSS-property comparisons (use `design_compare`); element-level cross-reference of clusters (use `design_audit`).

**Coordinate frame:** HTML viewport / image-pixel (1:1). All inputs (`ignoreRegions`, `alignOn.referenceRect`) and outputs (cluster bboxes, mask region rects) live here.

**Common misreads:**
- *Score reads "Diff: 5%" but `design_audit` reports 0.95* — that's `compare_element`'s diff-percent (lower better) vs `design_audit`'s `visualScore` (higher better). Both are correct, neither is wrong.
- *`alignOn.referenceRect` taken from Figma canvas* — `align-on-frame-mismatch`. Convert to viewport pixels first or use `alignTo: "top"|"center"` if the element-relative shortcut is what you wanted.
- *Mask covers everything; score is 99%* — `mask-pair-fabrication`. Re-run unmasked, report both. Honest score is the unmasked one.
- *Crop region exceeds reference image bounds* — pass `boundsHandling: "intersect"` to clamp, or use `alignTo`/`alignOn` to shift the reference origin.

### compare_screenshot {#surface-compare-screenshot}

**Available in mode:** `dev` plugin — always present.

**Authoritative for:** full-viewport (or `startY`/`endY`-clipped) live ↔ reference PNG comparison, no selector. Mask contract identical to `compare_element`.

**Not authoritative for:** element-anchored crops (use `compare_element`); CSS-property comparisons (use `design_compare`).

**Coordinate frame:** HTML viewport / image-pixel.

**Common misreads:**
- *"Image dimensions don't match" hard error* — viewport doesn't match the reference image's WxH. The tool requires equal dims; resize the reference, or use `compare_element` if you only care about a region.
- Same `mask-pair-fabrication` and score-convention misreads as `compare_element`.

### visual_diff {#surface-visual-diff}

**Available in mode:** `dev` plugin — always present.

**Authoritative for:** pixelmatch between two static PNGs, no browser launched. Optional `crop: true` auto-crops to the smaller of the two when dimensions differ. Useful as the final step in a manual capture-then-compare flow.

**Not authoritative for:** anything requiring live page state. No mask flags — preprocess the PNGs externally if you need masking.

**Coordinate frame:** image-pixel only.

**Common misreads:**
- *Used to verify a live page change* — `visual_diff` doesn't navigate. Use `compare_screenshot` or `compare_element` for live URL → reference flows.

### design_audit {#surface-design-audit}

**Available in mode:** `wordpress` (via `design-compare` plugin).

**Authoritative for:** end-to-end design compliance check. Runs `design_compare` (CSS property comparison) + visual diff + cross-references diff clusters back to named elements. Output groups clusters as `explained` (overlap an element with property mismatches), `excluded` (overlap a `knownExclusions` selector), or `unexplained`. `coverageManifest` enables element/property coverage stats.

**Not authoritative for:** raw pixelmatch (use `compare_screenshot`); element-cropped comparison (use `compare_element`); arbitrary CSS-property check without a design spec (use `computed_styles`).

**Coordinate frame:** HTML viewport. Element bboxes are reported relative to `rootSelector.boundingBox()` (subtracted) for cluster-cross-reference.

**Common misreads:**
- *Looking for `ignoreElements` / `ignoreText` / `ignoreRegions`* — `design_audit` doesn't have them. The analogue is `hideSelectors` (pre-screenshot suppression) and `knownExclusions` (post-hoc cluster classification, no visual effect).
- *`hiddenArea` value used as fraction* — it's a percentage (1 decimal). `hiddenArea > 25` is the SKILL gate threshold; `> 0.25` would mean a quarter of a percent.
- *Cluster cross-reference shows `unexplained` but builder fixed the property mismatch* — `design_compare` ran before the fix; re-run `design_audit` after the fix and the cluster classification will update.
- *Animation race not caught despite `freezeAnimations: true`* — this flag is `design_audit`-only. If the live page is on a different domain than the reference and the reference is loaded via `referenceUrl`, both sides need freeze; the flag injects on both.

### design_compare {#surface-design-compare}

**Available in mode:** `wordpress` (via `design-compare` plugin).

**Authoritative for:** CSS-property comparison live ↔ design spec. Tolerant numeric comparison (px tolerance, max 2px cap), color normalization, font-family primary comparison (parses fallback stack), pseudo-element support. No screenshots taken.

**Not authoritative for:** visual / pixel comparison (`design_audit` runs `design_compare` + visual; or use `compare_*` tools); coordinate-based checks beyond `bbox.width` / `bbox.height` (use `evaluate_script` for `getBoundingClientRect()`).

**Coordinate frame:** none — compares CSS values, not coordinates.

**Common misreads:**
- *Tolerance "2px" was passed but a 4px delta is reported as match* — tolerance silently caps at 2px (anti-gaming). The capped value is echoed in the output.
- *Font-family test fails despite the same font* — the comparison parses primary font from fallback stacks via `parseFontStack`. If both sides use the same primary, it matches. If you want exact-string match, pre-normalize.
- *Translation displacement (probe) doesn't move design_compare result* — `design_compare` checks the property list you supplied; if `transform` isn't in the list, displacement is invisible to it. The visual phase of `design_audit` is where displacement surfaces.

### list_modes {#surface-list-modes}

**Available in mode:** all (core primitive).

**Authoritative for:** enumeration of currently registered modes in this server process. Output reflects the env-var-loaded plugin set.

**Not authoritative for:** anything about plugins that aren't loaded. A skipped plugin produces no entry; the tool can't tell you "this would be present if you set `WP_URL`."

**Coordinate frame:** none.

**Common misreads:**
- *"No modes registered"* — `wp-mode-not-registered`. Plugin loader silently skipped one or more plugins for missing env. Stderr has the full list of skips. Add the missing var (typically `WP_URL`) and restart Claude Code (not just `/mcp` reconnect — env-only changes need a fresh session).

## Common workflows {#workflows}

### Compare a built block to a Figma reference

1. Have figexport export the block: produces `design-styles.json`, `selectors.json`, optionally `masked.png` + `masked.json`.
2. From the SKILL audit-config, build `elements: [{name, selector, expected}]` from `design-styles.json`.
3. Invoke `design_audit({rootSelector, elements, referenceImage, hideSelectors?, knownExclusions?, coverageManifest?})`.
4. Read `visualScore`, per-element results, and cluster cross-reference. Property mismatches surface in `elements[].results`; visual-only misses surface as `unexplained` clusters with `domHints`.
5. If `visualScore` is low and `unexplained` clusters exist, run a displacement probe (SKILL § 6.6 Empirical signal is truth) before invoking rendering / antialiasing explanations.

### Debug a low score on `compare_element`

1. Inspect `Mask coverage: N.N%` line. If > 60% with both broad flags, score is fabricated — re-run unmasked.
2. Inspect cluster annotations (`clusterAnnotations`) — these tell you which DOM elements overlap each diff cluster.
3. Run the displacement probe: `translate-y-[25px]` / `translate-y-[-25px]` / `[50px]` / `[-50px]` on the cited element. Predict the score direction first; observe.
4. If the score moves the wrong way, your premise is wrong (named: `horizontal-cards-y515`).
5. If the score doesn't move, the diff isn't measuring the cited element. Check `ignoreRegions` static rects, sibling drivers, or whether the element fell outside the crop / root.

### Open a persistent session for a multi-step flow

1. `open_session({browser: "chromium", viewport: {...}})` → returns `session_id`.
2. Pass `session_id` to every subsequent tool call.
3. `close_session({session_id})` when done. Sessions auto-touch on every call to keep them alive against the idle timeout.

## Diagnosis {#diagnosis}

Symptoms → causes → fixes for the failure modes that have shown up in real builds. Each entry is named for cross-doc grep.

### `wp-mode-not-registered` {#wp-mode-not-registered}

**Symptom:** `mcp__browser__list_modes` returns "No modes registered" or `wordpress` mode missing; every `wp_*` / `wp_gutenberg_*` tool comes back as deferred-but-unresolvable.

**Cause:** silent plugin skip from missing env. `wp` plugin requires `WP_URL`; if absent, `wp` is skipped, and `wp-gutenberg` cascade-skips because it depends on `wp`. The server boots cleanly, but the `wordpress` mode is never registered.

**Fix:** project's `.mcp.json` must have a `browser` server entry with full env block — MCP scopes replace, do not merge. Minimum: `BROWSER_MCP_PLUGINS=dev,wp,wp-gutenberg,design-compare`, `WP_URL=http://<project>.local`, optional `WP_USERNAME`/`WP_PASSWORD`. Full restart of Claude Code (not `/mcp` reconnect) to pick up env changes.

### `tolerant-load-cascade` {#tolerant-load-cascade}

**Symptom:** plugin A is loaded fine, plugin B (which depends on A's mode) is silently absent, no obvious error in `list_modes`.

**Cause:** A was skipped silently for missing env at registry-load time (commit 3a88385 made this skip non-fatal). B cascade-skips because A is its declared dependency.

**Fix:** check stderr from server boot for the skip reason. Address the missing env on A (or on a transitive dep further up). The cascade is deterministic — fixing the root unblocks all dependents.

### `mask-pair-fabrication` {#mask-pair-fabrication}

**Symptom:** `compare_element` or `compare_screenshot` reports `Match: YES` with `Diff: <1%` but the live page visibly doesn't match the reference. `Mask coverage: N.N%` is high.

**Cause:** `ignoreAllImages: true` and `ignoreText: true` simultaneously masked nearly all visible content. The remaining unmasked region is wrapper-background, which trivially matches.

**Fix:** re-run unmasked. Manifest's `score` field carries the unmasked number; masked-flag invocations live under `analyticalMasks[]` with the mask config attached. SKILL § 6.7 hard-fails masked-only filings.

### `align-on-frame-mismatch` {#align-on-frame-mismatch}

**Symptom:** `compare_element` `alignOn` reports a delta that exceeds 100px and triggers the warning, OR delta is small but the comparison drifts in a consistent direction.

**Cause:** `alignOn.referenceRect` provided in Figma canvas coordinates instead of HTML viewport / image-pixel coordinates. The conversion offset (canvas origin to rendered origin) absorbs into `deltaX`/`deltaY` and shifts the reference crop.

**Fix:** convert source coords first. The conversion lives at `../figexport/llms-full.txt#coordinate-spaces`. If you only need element-relative alignment, use `alignTo: "top"|"center"` instead of `alignOn` — `alignTo` doesn't take user-supplied coords.

### `horizontal-cards-y515` {#horizontal-cards-y515}

**Symptom:** live cards render at one Y, design source claims another; builder rationalizes the gap as JPG artifacts / antialiasing / cross-renderer subpixel differences.

**Cause:** the source-side coordinate value was misread (Figma layer coord vs rendered position vs unscaled-tree-md value).

**Fix:** displacement probe. `translate-y-[N]` toward the claimed target position; predict the score should improve; observe. If it gets worse, the target value was wrong. SKILL § 6.6 Empirical signal is truth; full treatment in P_new_3 of the SKILL draft. Cross-link figexport's source-frame discussion: `../figexport/llms-full.txt#coordinate-spaces`.

### `code-connect-advisory-as-empty-spec` {#code-connect-advisory-as-empty-spec}

**Symptom:** `design_compare` / `design_audit` audit-config has empty or default-valued expected properties; live page mismatches almost everything but no one noticed during build.

**Cause:** figexport-side. Builder read `code-connect.json` as "no spec exists" when the file actually carried an advisory marker (`"missing code connect mappings"` / `"design was too large to fit into context"`). figexport-canonical: cross-source to `design-context.{tsx,json}` or re-export. Full treatment at `../figexport/llms-full.txt#code-connect-advisory-as-empty-spec`.

**Fix (browser-mcp side, downstream):** when audit-config is suspiciously empty or expected values look like defaults, halt and re-run figexport before running `design_audit`. Don't ship a passing audit against an empty spec — it tells you nothing.

### `modal-shadow-miss` {#modal-shadow-miss}

**Symptom:** modal / overlay element renders without a box-shadow that the design specifies; `design_compare` doesn't catch it because `box-shadow` isn't in the audit config.

**Cause:** figexport-canonical. Tsx-side dropped the `effects[]` (MCP heuristic), json-side carries it. Builder-imported tsx as primary, missed the shadow. P_new_7 precedence: json wins for color/spacing/typography/effects.

**Fix:** ensure `box-shadow` (and other effects-derived properties) are in the `elements[].expected` list in the audit config. Sourced from `design-styles.json _meta.propertyCounts`. Cross-link figexport's full case: `../figexport/llms-full.txt#modal-shadow-miss`.

## Versioning {#versioning}

This document tracks `browser-mcp` main; for behavior at a specific commit see `git log src/`. Material contract changes (new fields, threshold tweaks) update this file in the same PR.

Stable as of commit `5078684` (maskCoverage on compare_element/compare_screenshot, parity with design_audit hiddenArea).
